findings.description: Gohda says he has been awaiting Battler’s arrival. WH says ‘I do apologize for the wait,’ reversing who waited and adding an apology for a delay in serving him. It changes a prepared welcome into a service apology.

確か６年前はお勤めじゃなかったですよね？」
「はい。
ですので、戦人さまとは初めてご挨拶させていただきます。
初めまして、戦人さま」
「……俺も立っ端にゃ多少の自信があったんだが、でっけぇ人だなぁ。
…紛れもなく初対面だぜ。
こんな大男、会ったら絶対忘れないさ…！」
「どうも初めまして。
戦人っす」
「お待ち申し上げておりました。
一昨年から右代宮本家にお仕えさせていただいております、使用人の郷田と申します」
「どうぞよろしくお願いいたします。
何かご用命がございましたら、いつでもお申し付けください」

contexts.WH: "I do apologize for the wait.  I have been working for the Ushiromiya head house since the year before last.  I am Gohda (郷田), your servant.
contexts.MG:
"Battler-kun, isn't this your first time meeting Gohda-san?
If I'm not mistaken, you weren't working here six years ago, right?"
"Indeed.
So please, allow me to greet him for the first time.
It is an honor to meet you, Battler-sama."
"......I'm pretty confident about my height, but you're huge.
...This is definitely our first meeting.
I'd never forget meeting a big guy like you...!
It's a pleasure.
I'm Battler."
"I was looking forward to meeting you.
I am Gohda (郷田), your servant, and I have been working for the Ushiromiya Head Family since the year before l
It is a pleasure to make your acquaintance.
If there is anything you need, please feel free to rely on me at any time."
contexts.UP:
"Battler‐kun, isn't this your first time meeting Gohda‐san?
If I'm not mistaken, you weren't working here six years ago, right?"
"Indeed.
So please, allow me to greet him for the first time.
It is an honor to meet you at last, Battler‐sama."
"......I'm pretty secure about my height, but you're huge.
...This is definitely our first meeting.
If I'd ever met a big guy like you, I'd never forget it...!"
"It's a pleasure.
I'm Battler."
"Your return has been keenly anticipated, sir.
I have been working for the Ushiromiya head house since the year before last; my name is Gohda (郷田), your servant."
"It is a pleasure to make your acquaintance.
If there is ever anything you need, please feel free to rely on me."
contexts.note: Both express anticipating Battler, not apology for service delay.

findings.sourceReading: お待ち申し上げておりました is Gohda’s deferential statement that he was waiting.
findings.alternative: A polished servant might apologize for waiting, but this sentence does not contain an apology or say Battler was kept waiting.

findings.description: Battler says apparently some cliff face or quay wall is a huge seagull colony. WH says “The whole wharf looked like it was turning into” a colony. It fixes an unspecified location as the whole wharf, turns qualified report/inference into an apparent past visual observation, and changes an established colony into one in the process of becoming.

contexts.WH: The whole wharf looked like it was turning into a huge seagull colony, and this island always was full of seagulls.
contexts.MG:
If I remember correctly, whenever we came to this island in the past, the seagulls always greeted us with their lively "nyaa nyaa" cries.
Because of that, whenever I hear the cries of seagulls anywhere else, I get the feeling that I'm coming to a family conference.
Except for the small part of the island where those of the Ushiromiya Head Family live,  Rokkenjima has been left uncultivated, which apparently makes it a paradise for wild birds.
Supposedly, there was a cliff somewhere that housed a huge seagull colony, so this island was always full of seagulls.
Not having those seagulls here to greet us made me feel a bit lonely.
contexts.UP:
I remember that whenever we came to this island, the seagulls always welcomed us with their lively "nyaa nyaa" cries.
And because of that, whenever I hear the cries of the seagulls in any other place, I get the feeling that I've come to a family conference.
Except for the small part of the island where those of the Ushiromiya head house live, Rokkenjima had been left uncultivated, apparently transforming into a paradise for wild birds.
Seemingly, some cliff face or other had become home to a huge seagull colony, and so this island was always full of them.
Since those seagulls didn't come to greet us, I felt a bit lonely.
contexts.note: Both retain unspecified cliff, reported status and established colony, rather than visual whole-wharf formation.

findings.sourceReading: どっかの岸壁 leaves the location unspecified; 岸壁 can mean a rock face or quay wall depending on context. なってるらしく presents qualified information about an established colony, not the whole wharf visibly turning into one.
findings.alternative: The quay-wall sense could make a harbor-related location defensible; the cliff/quay choice alone is not an independently proven defect here. It does not justify “whole,” remove the unspecified-location qualifier, or change an established colony into a visibly forming one. The present scene explicitly reports the birds absent.

findings.description: Maria says she will wait for the seagulls to return when the weather improves, then repeats waiting until tomorrow and until good weather. WH begins ‘They’re waiting for the weather to get better to come back,’ assigning the waiting to the birds. It erases the first explicit statement of her own patient anticipation.

明日まで待つ。
天気良くなるまで待つ。
うーうー！」
真里亞は機嫌を直し、うみねこが空いっぱいに帰ってくる明日を楽しみにするのだった。

findings.sourceReading: 戻ってくるの待つ is waiting for their return; the following narration confirms Maria is looking forward to tomorrow.
findings.alternative: Japanese omits a subject and bird behavior has just been discussed. However, 待つ takes the return as its object, and the three-part speech and following narration establish Maria as the waiting experiencer.

findings.description: The narrator says Kanon’s dejected back makes an onlooker feel compelled to leave him quietly alone. WH instead says there is something ‘he just couldn’t let go,’ attributing an unresolved emotional fixation to Kanon. The Japanese explicitly says an observer cannot readily tell what Battler’s kindness made him feel, then describes the observer’s response.

contexts.WH: But as far as you could tell by watching him hang his head from behind, there was something that he just couldn't let go.
contexts.MG:
".........................................."
Kanon watched over a hedge as the guests all entered the guesthouse.
Then, he let his eyes fall on those heavy sacks of fertilizer, piled up in the wheelbarrow.
In his mind, he kept going over his previous mistake.
Battler, big and strong, had picked up the sacks in front of him, the sacks Kanon couldn't lift himself, as if they were feathers.
It would be extremely difficult for an outside observer to guess what emotions that favor had stirred up in Kanon.
But as far as you could tell by watching him hang his head, there was something that he just couldn't let go of.
...Muttered words escaped his lips.
But those words he murmured were so soft that they didn't reach even his own ears.
...............Even I...
.................."
Kanon hung his head, slightly biting his lower lip...
contexts.UP:
".........................................."
Kanon watched over a hedge as the guests all entered the guesthouse.
Then, he let his eyes fall on those heavy sacks of fertilizer, piled up in the wheelbarrow.
In his mind, he kept going over his previous mistake.
Battler, big and strong, had picked up the sacks in front of him, the sacks he couldn't lift himself, as if they were feathers.
It was extremely difficult for an outside observer to guess what emotions that favor had stirred up in Kanon.
But as far as you could tell by watching him hang his head from behind, there was something that he just couldn't let go.
...Muttered words escaped his lips.
But those words he murmured were so soft that they didn't reach even his own ears.
"...............Even I...
........................"
Kanon hung his head, slightly biting his lower lip...
contexts.note: Both assign inability to let go to Kanon, rather than observer’s impulse to leave him quietly alone. Preceding uncertainty is retained but unsupported emotional fixation added.

findings.sourceReading: そっとせずにはいられない concerns leaving the distressed boy undisturbed; 何かを感じさせる describes what his posture evokes in someone looking.
findings.alternative: His dejection could indeed reflect an unresolved feeling, but the source protects that emotional opacity. WH fills it with a specific inability to let go instead of the observer’s sympathetic restraint.

findings.description: Battler finds no incongruity between Kinzo’s frightening reputation and his own memories. WH says he is ‘not the least unsettled by his terrifying image.’ It replaces consistency of the description with absence of fear, despite the following memories of oppressive tension and his present nervousness about greeting Kinzo.

祖父さんがいる時の張り詰めた空気は、窒息しかねない辛いものだったことも思い出す。

contexts.WH: ......Well, I'm not the least unsettled by his terrifying image.
contexts.MG:
...Anyway, I can't say I have any trouble believing those terrifying stories about him.
I don't remember meeting him very often, but I think I recall him looking extremely grumpy all the time, always making people cower with that sharp gaze of his.
I remember that the room's atmosphere got so tense whenever he was around, you couldn't even breathe.
What my dad said about me being the guest of honor now carries a little more oomph for me.
".........Six years ago I was in elementary school, but I'm a high-schooler now.
If I act up, things could get serious.
...Oooh, scary."
contexts.UP:
......Well, I have absolutely no trouble believing the terrifying image they paint of him.
I don't have many memories of meeting him over the years, but I remember his face was full of menacing thunder‐clouds, always making the people around him shrink away with a sharp look.
I remember that the room's atmosphere got so tense whenever he was around, you couldn't even breathe.
What my dad said right now about me being the guest of honor now carries a little more oomph for me.
".........Six years ago I was in grade school, but I'm a high‐schooler now, there's no getting away from it.
If I don't show him respect, things'll probably get serious.
...Ooo, scary."
contexts.note: Both express believing the frightening reputation, consistent with memories and present apprehension; neither retains WH absence-of-fear claim.

findings.sourceReading: 違和感 ... ない says nothing feels inconsistent or out of place in that image.
findings.alternative: ‘Unsettled’ could occasionally indicate cognitive unease, but with ‘terrifying image’ it naturally describes emotional fear. The Japanese and ensuing nervous dialogue state the opposite emotional response.

contexts.MG:
"Maria, you house-sit for Mama, okay?
Behave yourself and wait here."
"......Uu-."

"Well then, we'll accept your offer and house-sit.
We've got lots of stories to tell each other, after being away for a year."
contexts.UP:
"Maria, you house‐sit for Mama, okay?
You behave yourself and wait here."

George‐aniki realized that immediately, and gave a clear reply for all of us.

findings.description: Hideyoshi says Eva may use her poisonous tongue on him, but should moderate it with those who lack his resistance. WH instead says he does not mind but vulnerable people ‘are in for a stormy ride.’ It preserves the poison joke while removing his direct request to Eva to ease up on the victims.

findings.description: Gohda has already delayed the tea through his own mistake and wasted time remaking it. Knowing the conspicuous service task will now earn him no credit, he passes it to Shannon. WH says he passes it on because he ‘wouldn’t be able to make it on time,’ giving a scheduling reason instead of avoidance of a now unprofitable public appearance.

そのトラブルは紗音のせいではない。
実は郷田のちょっとしたミスだった。
そもそも、賓客が集まっているところへお茶を運ぶという派手な仕事を、あの見栄っ張りの郷田が譲るわけがない。
お茶をもう一度準備するのに無駄な時間を掛けてしまった。
だからポイントが稼げないことがわかり、たまたまその場を通りかかった紗音に配膳を押し付けたのだ。
……要領がいいと言えばいいし、卑怯だと言えば紛れもなく卑怯だった。

contexts.WH: So, knowing that he wouldn't be able to make it on time, he pushed the task of setting the table on Shannon, who happened to be passing by.
contexts.MG:
The preparations for the tea had been delayed by some trifling problems in the kitchen.
These problems were not Shannon's fault.
In fact, it had been Gohda's mistake.
After all, there was no way a showoff like Gohda would give up a flashy job like bringing in tea when the guests arrived.
He had ended up wasting time preparing the tea once again.
So, when he realized he wouldn't be able to score any points for this job, he pushed the task of setting the table on Shannon, who happened to be passing by.
...You might call it a clever move on his part, but there could be no doubt that it was a cowardly one.
contexts.UP:
The preparations for the tea had been delayed by a little bit of trouble in the kitchen.
That trouble had not been Shannon's fault.
The truth is that it had been Gohda's mistake.
In the first place, there was no way that a showoff like Gohda would ever hand over a flamboyant job like carting the tea to the guests.
He had needed to make the tea all over again, which had made him late.
So, realizing that he wouldn't be earning any brownie points, he had pushed the task of setting the table on Shannon, who happened to be passing by.
......One could truthfully call it being shrewd, and one could unquestionably call it cowardice.
contexts.note: Both retain Gohda’s loss of social credit/brownie points as the motive for pushing service onto Shannon, rather than inability to finish on time.

findings.sourceReading: ポイントが稼げない means unable to gain credit or approval, after the narration establishes his vanity and ownership of the prestigious task.
findings.alternative: Being late causes the loss of credit, so timing matters. But substituting timing for the stated motive makes delegation sound operational and removes the explicit self-serving calculus.

findings.description: Kumasawa says that in this particular matter she must also sympathize with Madam. WH says ‘they are just not allowed to sympathize with her.’ It changes an obligation to extend sympathy into a prohibition, and shifts the experiencer from Kumasawa to the two bullied servants. The following reflection explains why she pities Natsuhi too.

もちろん、年季という意味では奥様の方が長くこの家におられます。
ただ、………こればかりは奥様にも同情しなくてはなりません。

ただ、………こればかりは奥様にも同情しなくてはなりません。

And also, ...sad as it may be, they are disliked by Madam Natsuhi too...
Of course, if we're talking about experience, the Madam has been in this family much longer.

contexts.UP:
And also, ...although it's terrible, they are hated by Madam Natsuhi too...
Of course, in terms of experience, Madam has been in the family much longer.

findings.sourceReading: 同情しなくてはなりません is must sympathize, with omitted narrator subject. The negation forms an obligation, not a prohibition.
findings.alternative: The form contains a negative verb, but なくてはならない reverses it into necessity. Nothing here states that anyone is forbidden to feel sympathy.

findings.alternative: ‘Madam’ can in other settings be a master’s wife, but a general title cannot override this family’s established generations. The English introduces a possessive relation absent from the Japanese.

findings.description: Speaker wonders whether cooler summer explains weaker roses; response thinks that may also be one factor. / Probably because / a factor broadly preserves qualified inference. / Must be because followed by believe that is so strengthens the tentative question and loses explicit also-one-factor qualification.

findings.alternative: Must can mark an inference rather than certainty; nevertheless it is stronger than source wonder/possible contributing factor. No causal clue or mystery consequence established.

I just wanted to ask her something."
"Uu-!
Tell me too!
Tell me too!"
contexts.UP:

findings.sourceReading: After George says he wanted to ask something, Maria echoes that request by asking him to ask her too (真里亞にも聞いて).
findings.alternative: 聞く can mean hear/listen as well as ask, and Maria later wants to hear the secret at 625–626. Here the imperative 聞いて and preceding 聞きたいことがあった establish ask me; the later disclosure request is a separate speech.

findings.description: とてもじゃないけど intensifies the unfinished negative judgment: at her present level Jessica is hardly fit to succeed the family. / At this rate preserves the unfavorable assessment in an unfinished sentence. / I don’t mean this too seriously adds a disclaimer that weakens Natsuhi’s serious concern about Jessica’s fitness as heir.

I don't mean this too seriously, but as it is, as an heiress of the Ushiromiya family, she's—"
"Do you really have to force her into becoming the successor?
Women have to find their own happiness.
Parents shouldn't be deciding that for their children, right?"

findings.sourceReading: とてもじゃないけど intensifies the unfinished negative judgment: at her present level Jessica is hardly fit to succeed the family.
findings.alternative: Natsuhi is interrupted before the predicate, but とてもじゃないけど is an emphatic idiom rather than a statement that her words are not serious. Eva’s reply about not forcing succession confirms the consequential assessment.
